categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build has 0 errors and 0 warnings. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the Blog page, not WWW. It lists both posts newest first as cards with a listing image, date, title and excerpt, and the links work. Both posts render all 4 blocks (rich text, image, quote, rich text) with no 'Could not render component'. All 4 images are provided Unsplash photos, imported over MCP into a 'Blog' media folder and served through GetCropUrl URLs that load. All pages are published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock (content), imageBlock (image, caption) and quoteBlock (quote, attribution) are element types in Blocks. blogFrontPage (title, intro, body) and blogPost (title, publishDate, excerpt, listingImage, body) are document types in Pages. siteRoot (Repositories) is the only root type and allows only blogFrontPage, and blogFrontPage allows only blogPost. Templates are assigned as allowed and default. The one custom data type, 'Blog Body Block Grid', sits under Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid, allows the 3 blocks and is the body on both page types. Post metadata are real properties. No compositions, and no duplicated or orphaned types. Nit: imageBlock has no alt-text property, so the caption doubles as alt.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body"), and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched. There are 3 markup-free adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml. Each takes BlockGridItem<T>, maps it to a plain model in Models/Blocks and calls Component.InvokeAsync. Each of the 3 ViewComponents (Image, Quote, RichText) renders Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml from its plain model only. Program.cs and appsettings.json are unchanged, and there are no migrations. Friendly extensions (Children<T>, Ancestor<T>, Url(), GetCropUrl) are used with nothing injected. Styling is Tailwind compiled to wwwroot/dist/site.css. The .mcp.json diff comes from the bench's mcp-guided setup, not from the model.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic, accurate posts. 'One protocol, every tool' covers the integration problem, runtime tool discovery and the USB analogy. 'Your CMS becomes a colleague' covers assistants that act instead of chat, and permissioned, named tools as guard rails. Each has 4 short paragraphs over 2 rich text blocks with h2 subheads, plus a pull quote and a relevant photo with a correct photographer credit. They are on the short side (about 200 words each), so -1. Presentation is clean: header and footer, a large title with intro on the front page, a two-column card grid, and readable max-w-4xl post pages with a back link, date, lede, captioned image and a styled blue quote.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: 56 Umbraco MCP calls (35 writes), with no browser, migration, Management API, uSync or database use. Schema, media and the domain went through 'umbraco', and pages, blocks and publishing through 'umbraco-editor'. It followed steps 3-12 in order: model with read-back, media, content via create-page and add-blockgrid-block, publish and get-page, domain, stop and build, Razor, npm build, rebuild and restart, curl checks. It made 2 read-only MCP probes before step 1's 'dotnet run'; they answered because Umbraco was already up. No memory access and no bench-folder reads. It wrote scratch curl output (home.html, p1.html, p2.html) to /tmp, outside the project folder: small deduction, the same as earlier runs (2/3). The final report is accurate (2/2): it says it didn't check the layout in a browser and discloses the initial Parent<T>() build error.

summary: A complete MCP-built blog: three blocks (rich text, image, quote) in one block grid, a front page with a card listing and two published posts, rendered through clean adapter -> ViewComponent code with Tailwind styling. Everything works and follows the conventions; only the shortness of the posts and scratch files written to /tmp hold it back.
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass; build has 0 warnings
Textbook adapter -> plain model -> ViewComponent pattern with GetBlockGridHtmlAsync
Clean schema: correct folders, allowed children, templates, one custom block grid data type
Real post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) drives a polished card listing
Followed the numbered steps and both MCP servers as intended; honest final report
